specs.value: Dark multi-mineral nutrient substrate (base layer) for freshwater planted aquariums, built on Deponit-Mix Professional
Rock material (75% basalt and lava), high-moor peat (H3–H5), bentonite clay
P2O5 84 mg/L; K2O 1,064 mg/L; Mg 182 mg/L; contains boron and zinc
None added; montmorillonite clay buffers nutrients
At least 8 years (stated by retailer for 4.8 kg bag)

fits.fact: Made to go under dark or black gravel. Its colour stays hidden even when the gravel cap is thin.
Freshwater planted tanks only. It feeds plants through their roots.
One buyer said it looks truly black, has an even grain and works well under JBL Sansibar Black sand.
A Dennerle Nano Cube 60 needs about 3–4 L of it, depending on how thick the layer is.
The shop's Q&A says it can also go under aqua soil as a base layer.

usage.fact: Spread 1.5–3 cm on the tank floor, then cap it with 3.5–6 cm of gravel.
Wet the substrate thoroughly before you plant.
Fill the tank slowly with water at about 20 °C. Only then switch on the filter, heater and light.
It must stay under an inert cap of gravel or sand. It is not meant to be the top layer.

issues.fact: It works like Deponit-Mix Professional, but it has no white activator beads, so it stays dark.

Shops use different names for it (Deponit Mix Black, Deponit-Mix Black 10in1). Dennerle also sells a newer 1 kg 'Deponit Mix Pro Black' with a different recipe (lava, peat, bentonite/montmorillonite, pH 6.8). Don't mix the two up.
Stock varies. A Hungarian shop had the 2.4 kg out of stock, and its 9.6 kg was last sold in January 2024.

alternatives.why: Same base recipe in a lighter colour, with activator beads. Greendeal.vn lists 2.4 kg at 290,000₫, 4.8 kg at 450,000₫ and 9.6 kg at 690,000₫, but all sizes were sold out when checked.
Slow-release base layer with no nitrate or phosphate, in 2.5 L and 5 L bags. It lasts about 2–3 years and can be recharged with liquid fertiliser, so it is a shorter-lived but cheaper option.
